front.title: SCIM User Supersession and Identity Resolution Correction Events

abstract.t: The System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) defines resources, provisioning operations, and Security Event Token (SET) based events for resource lifecycle changes. Existing standardized SCIM events can signal that a User resource was created, modified, activated, deactivated, or deleted, but they do not express an identity-resolution decision in which one User resource is retired in favor of another User resource representing the same subject within the issuer's authority. Deletion and supersession have different semantics for downstream systems. This document defines two SCIM provisioning events: a User supersession event and a supersession- correction event. It distinguishes resource supersession from identity-attribute convergence and specifies how ordinary SCIM provisioning events communicate the resulting authoritative SCIM state of the surviving User. Matching algorithms, attribute- convergence and conflict-resolution policy, identity proofing, and non-SCIM data handling remain outside the scope of this document. Pre-authentication and pseudonymous profile linkage is identified as related future work but is not standardized by this document.
